title: Failed native file operations are misclassified as malformed lifecycles; shared provider state needs explicit node binding
backend: Codex tool_rich_candidate_v1 and experiment node transport

evidence.event_indices: Old 021 stdout indices 4/5, 6/7, 8/9 are stable started/completed file_change pairs with final status failed; candidate file was not produced. M3 successor repeats failed file operations and reports an absent .codex/tmp/arg0/.../codex-linux-sandbox. M2 resumed qualification exits with list_turns is not supported yet (code -32601).

observation: The adapter only allows status completed for file changes despite retaining failed command/tool statuses. Thus a well-formed failed operation hides the actual file-write failure. Both hosts share the same HOME under /mnt/b300-shared; helper disappearance and resume failure motivate testing explicit node-local Codex state, but do not prove a single root cause. A deterministic sandbox /bin/true probe succeeds on both nodes; M2 also reports stale arg0 cleanup failure. Old 003 has serial GPU evaluation receipts and is not proven stuck.
proposed_change: Retain failed file-change status without changing payload/lifecycle checks or candidate file postconditions; absent/invalid candidates still fail. Permit a validated, explicitly provisioned per-node codex_home in experiment inputs, forwarded only to that node launcher and preserved across initial/resume. Keep sandbox workspace-write and the current binary/model. Validate with raw replay and a fresh two-turn qualification before new runs. Never rewrite old failed outcomes.

verified_by.kind: software and retained original JSONL replay
verified_by.outcome: Both original raw streams parse with failed file statuses retained; candidate absence still refuses acceptance. Old failures remain failed.
verified_by.scope: Protocol parsing repair only. Node-local state mitigation and live recovery require new qualification.
